questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Language, security and university life

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty simple, my coordinator made sure to stay in touch and give me all the necessary information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nothing in particular

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Pretty simple, I used the ESN groupchat where some of the people who had been at my destination before me were making us aware of available rooms.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Its nice, it gives you a break from the univeristy, for my destination everything was close by as well so it was a very easy place to navigate.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I recieved an email well in advance from my coordinator in Salamanca so I knew what to do as soon as I arrived. We scheduled a meeting to sign the necessary documents and to sign me up for my courses with the secretary.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I mainly used communication via email nothing else was needed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would just say do it, dont stress it and live within the city centre its close to all faculties. Also remember a pen and paper its old fashioned.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was fine, I think it suited the BA-level however as many of the ccourses were 4,5-6 ECTS they put too many things into one class compared to the amount of points recieved.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I prefer UCPH, its more engaging and the teachers seem more passionate about what they are teaching. The teaching style in Salamanca was more dry, as if they were teaching because they had to and not because they wanted. However, the teachers were nice and sympathetic but the teaching style felt more stiff.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Semántica y pragmática
Lingüística textual y análisis del discurso
Ética I
Estética de las creaciones literarias
Filosofís II: Conceptos fundamentales

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all of them actually, to highlight some it would be: Lingüística textual (the teaching style and exam is more simular to what the students at UCPH might be used to), estética de las creaciones literarias (teaching style is similar to UCPH but a lot of theory) and ética (simple, a lot of assignements so everything wont depend on the exam)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None, I had to buy a second suitcase but other than that none.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: eating out was much cheaper than anticipated, groceries however were more expensive than I initially thought.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I am not aware of anything hosted by the university, except for all the posters I saw on the wall. But the ESN-community was very active and had activities almost daily. Also the city had nice places for running, chilling, getting coffee or going out.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the ESN groupchat and participate in the first activities it will give you a solid base of friends so you wont feel lonely. Say yes, try (except if its really stupid and dangerous)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Find the main attractions in the very beginning to get to know the city and allow yourself to fall in love with it, and for Salamanca specifically; go clubbing you dont have to drink but it is a great way to meet new people and find friends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, people are kind, helpful and easygoing, imitating what and how they do things and go from there.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It is difficult, however helpful if they know you speak their language and also live in a shared apartment or in a residence in that way you will get to know them other than just academically.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Walking the streets, because people dont make space or move as we do in the north, if they want to stop they stop, if you walk where they want to and you dont move, you will bump into eachother.
Not washing hands or covering the mouth when sneezing and coughing – very disgusting and it took some time (and colds) to get used to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The slow pace, taking the time to talk and relax and not stress about life. And siesta.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Enjoy it, the people are amazing, the food is great and the lifestyle is to die for
Live in the city center so you can walk anywhere also at night
Accept that univeristy is different from what you are used to, eventhough UCPH probably does it better.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met, without them everything would have been different.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Accepting the way of teaching and how it was more about memorizing than learning and thinking.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
